summary: Iter163 — Regression + new-feature test of evidence_feedback tracking extended to uploaded-document evidence and the new Super Admin Low-Accuracy Alert panel. Backend: 9/9 pytest cases pass (doc-upload PUT single evidence writes evidence_feedback with upload_id set / meeting_id NULL; doc-upload bulk-action writes N rows matching changed_count; meeting evidence PUT still writes meeting_id-based rows with upload_id NULL — no regression from the m033 schema change; super-admin/ai-accuracy-report is 403 for admin role, 200 for super_admin, every item has source_type∈{meeting,document} + source_label + upload_id/meeting_id mutually exclusive, by_org totals include document decisions, org/action/date filters work). Frontend (after `sudo supervisorctl restart frontend` — the prod build was serving stale JS from the previous session): (a) 'Source' column header confirmed (was 'Meeting'), (b) each row shows a 'MEETING' or 'DOCUMENT' tag under the link, (c) meeting-row link → /meetings/{id}/report, document-row link → /doc-uploads/{id} (verified in source, meeting variant verified in DOM), (d) new Low-Accuracy Alert panel (data-testid `ai-accuracy-low-alerts`) is HIDDEN when no org qualifies (Test Company at 99.4% and no other orgs had ≥5 decisions), then verified APPEARS after seeding an 8-decided/25%-acceptance scenario in 'New test Scotland' — panel rendered '1 organisation below 90% acceptance' with row 'New test Scotland — 25% acceptance (2/8 decided)' and correct data-testid `ai-accuracy-low-alert-510e66b2-6f78-4bb5-aea0-bf19663f1c3a`, (e) existing By-Organisation red-highlight at <60% is unchanged (seeded 25% row rendered red; Test Company 99.4% row is not red for AR). All seeded rows cleaned up + upload mapping baseline restored to (21 pending, 2 accepted, 1 rejected) exactly as noted in the review request.
critical_code_review_comments: Data-integrity note (not user-facing but worth a defensive CHECK constraint): evidence_feedback now has both meeting_id and upload_id nullable and neither is NOT NULL — a bug could silently insert a row with BOTH NULL and the AI Accuracy report would render it as a broken 'Untitled meeting → /meetings/null/report' link (reproduced by direct SQL insert during test setup; not reachable via the API code paths — both review.py and doc_uploads.py always set one). Recommend adding `CHECK ((meeting_id IS NOT NULL) <> (upload_id IS NOT NULL))` in a follow-up migration to lock this invariant at the DB level.

super_admin.py ai_accuracy_report items query has LIMIT 200 hardcoded — fine for MVP visualization but the stats/by_org aggregates are un-limited so the log table can silently misrepresent the full population once an org crosses ~200 recent decisions. No functional bug today, just something to keep in mind before shipping to a >5-org customer base; consider adding paging or a total-count hint.

review.py's INSERT into evidence_feedback still lists 14 columns and does not list upload_id (relies on the column default NULL from m033). Works correctly (verified: meeting rows have upload_id IS NULL after my test) but the two files (review.py vs doc_uploads.py) now have divergent INSERT statements — a future refactor should extract a shared helper to keep the schema drift risk minimal.
